title: Time-windowed hysteresis generator for demand-anchored scaling targets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a deterministic policy component that synthesizes per-tenant scaling targets using demand-anchored statistics and time-windowed hysteresis. This component should produce conservative, explainable target values and a small set of safety signals (quarantine, backoff, forced-stability) consumable by the autoscaler core. The aim is to reduce oscillation, limit overprovision during short spikes, and ensure graceful decommit behavior when load drops.
background: Current autoscaler uses single-point percentile estimates with fixed step limits; we observe frequent oscillation for tenant workloads with bursty short spikes and slow drifting baselines. Existing mitigations (longer cooldowns, large step limits) either increase latency SLO breaches or waste capacity. Several recent incidents showed churn in dedicated fleets when multiple tenants simultaneously ramped and then dropped load.
goals: Produce stable per-tenant scale targets that honor committed throughput contracts
Suppress transient spikes shorter than a configurable window without blocking legitimate sustained growth
Provide transparent signals for safety actions (surge_quarantine, step_backoff, freeze_decommit)
Keep decision logic auditable and parameterizable by ops and product teams
proposal_summary: Implement a Time-windowed Hysteresis Generator (THG) that computes a robust target using a demand-anchored quantile estimator over multiple time windows (short/med/long). Combine outputs via conservative fusion: prefer long-window estimates unless short-window > threshold * long-window for > sustained-window duration. Apply derivative damping and capped step sizes, and emit safety signals when anomalies are detected (e.g., sustained high-derivative across tenants, sample-skew indicating synthetic load).
detailed_proposal: Input signals: per-tenant observed effective throughput (tokens/sec), median latency P95, queue depth, and model-variant occupancy.
Estimators: compute EMQ (exponential moving quantile) at 3 horizons: 1m (short), 10m (medium), 60m (long) with tunable smoothing constants.

Fusion rule: baseline = long_EMQ; if medium_EMQ > baseline * 1.15 for continuous > 5m then baseline = medium_EMQ; if short_EMQ > baseline * 1.25 for continuous > 10m then baseline = short_EMQ. These multipliers are conservative by default and configurable per tenant tier.
Hysteresis: enforce entry and exit windows with asymmetric thresholds to avoid flip-flop. Use separate entry_threshold and exit_threshold multipliers.
Derivative dampening: limit scale-up velocity by a leaky-integrator on target delta with configurable max_step_per_minute and recovery_curve for decommit.

Safety signals: emit 'surge_quarantine' when observed short_EMQ >> long_EMQ and concurrency spike is > 3x baseline; emit 'freeze_decommit' when decommit would violate retention SLOs for pinned sessions; emit 'step_backoff' if downstream queueing or model-variant saturation is detected.
Explainability: produce a compact rationale blob (string tags) like 'long-baseline', 'short-sustained', 'deriv-capped' for each target decision to show in the Console.
API: THG exposes an RPC: compute_target(tenant_id, recent_samples) -> {target_units, reason_tags, safety_flags}.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Aggressive smoothing reduces oscillation but can increase latency during sustained growth — mitigated via medium-window promotion rules.
Reactive stepper-only approach is simpler but fails to capture multi-timescale patterns and is more brittle under correlated tenant surges.
ML-based predictive approach was considered (short-term forecasting) but deferred due to training/data lifecycle and the desire for deterministic, auditable rules for early rollout.
We keep configuration per-tenant-tier to balance risk/cost (e.g., P0 customers get lower multipliers and faster promotion).
acceptance_criteria: THG prototype implemented in the autoscaler policy module and feature-flagged off by default
Unit and integration tests covering edge cases: short spike suppression, sustained growth promotion, derivative caps
Canary rollout to 10 tenants (mix of bursty and steady) demonstrates 40% reduction in scale-flip events vs baseline over 7 days
At most 5% increase in latency SLO breach rate for canary tenants during rollout window
Console shows per-target rationale tags and safety_flags for every decision in a human-readable format

testing_plan: Unit tests for EMQ estimator edge cases and window decay behavior
Integration test against autoscaler simulator that replays historical tenant traces and synthetic bursts
Closed-canary: deploy to 10 low-risk tenants for 7 days with aggressive telemetry and alerting
A/B test against baseline autoscaler for 4 weeks measuring scale-flip rate and SLO impact
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout in three phases: local QA -> closed canary (10 tenants) -> staged expansion (25%, 50%, 100%) with automatic rollback on guardrail violations (scale_flip_rate increases > 10% or latency_p95 regression > 5%).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: overly conservative targets increase SLO latency. Mitigation: medium-window promotion and explicit latency budget check before dampening.
Risk: correlated tenant behavior could trigger simultaneous promotions. Mitigation: global coordinator that enforces fleet-wide headroom cap and emits early warning alerts.
Risk: config complexity leads to mis-tuning. Mitigation: sensible defaults, tier presets, and observable rationale tags for debugging.
Risk: excessive telemetry cardinality. Mitigation: aggregate reason_tags histograms instead of storing full strings for every decision.
